scenes.title: Regions, Zones & Availability
scenes.narration: Cloud providers divide the world into regions and availability zones so you can place data close to users and survive hardware failures.

scenes.title: The Building Blocks
bullets: A region is a geographic area, such as us-east-1, containing multiple isolated data centers.
An availability zone is one or more data centers within a region with independent power and networking.
Placing resources across zones protects your pipelines when a single data center goes down.
scenes.narration: A region is a broad geographic location, and each region is made of several availability zones. Those zones have separate power and networking, so a failure in one rarely takes down another. Spreading critical resources across zones is the foundation of building fault-tolerant data systems.

scenes.title: Why Location Matters
scenes.narration: Where you deploy affects three things at once. Placing data near users lowers latency and improves responsiveness. Regulations may legally require data to stay in a country, and prices differ from region to region, so location is also a cost decision.

scenes.title: Region vs. Availability Zone
scenes.narration: The region answers where in the world your workload lives, driven by latency and compliance. The availability zone answers how you survive local failures within that region. Together they let you design for both proximity and resilience.

scenes.text: Pick a region for latency and compliance, then spread across availability zones for resilience — this simple habit prevents most single-point failures.
scenes.narration: Choose your region based on users and regulations, then distribute across zones to withstand outages. That two-step habit eliminates the most common single points of failure.
